reading: The small loose shape is removed and redrawn inside the 6-outline: its 2x2 pattern is stretched to the frame interior (a filled cell becomes a full side or corner region; a full 2x2 fills the interior).

slots.frame: interior of the one rectangular outline object
slots.placement: shape cells at the 2x2 box corners map to interior corners; lines between filled corners are drawn along the interior sides

why: the interior shows the shape's pattern scaled to the interior size; the original shape is erased

reading: Scale the grid by k = number of distinct non-background colours, then draw colour-2 diagonals outward from each corner of the inner square object until they hit a non-background cell or the edge.

slots.subject: the square object off the border strips
slots.rays: diagonals from its four box corners, colour 2, stop at obstacle or border

why: output = k-times enlarged input plus 2-diagonals from the square's corners

reading: Cells sit only on odd rows/columns; keep the 5x5 grid of odd positions and enlarge each cell to a 4x4 block (20x20 output).
why: output block (i,j) of size 4x4 has the colour of input cell (2i+1, 2j+1)

reading: Take the shape in the top-left panel (cut by the cross separator), recolour it with the separator colour, and mirror it into all four quadrants of an output that drops the separator.

slots.layout: unit, its horizontal flip, vertical flip, and 180-rotation as the four quadrants

why: output is 4-fold mirror-symmetric and its top-left quadrant is the top-left panel shape in the separator colour

reading: Swap the foreground colour with background 0 (invert the grid), then tile the inverted grid 2x2.
why: every output block equals the colour-inverted input

reading: Cut the 3x3 window holding the 8-shape and repeat it side by side once per colour-4 marker in the input.

slots.unit: 3x3 window around the 8-shape (bottom-aligned when the shape is only 2 rows tall)

why: output is 3 x 3N with N = number of 4-cells, each 3x3 block the same shape window

reading: Vertical 8-segments have lengths 2,4,6,8,10; the half of one segment coloured 9 goes back to 8, and the same half (top or bottom) of the next-longer segment becomes 9.

slots.source: vertical segment containing 9 (half of it is 9)
slots.target: the vertical segment whose length is the next larger value
slots.mark: same half (top/bottom) of the target recoloured 9; source restored to 8

why: exactly one segment carries 9 on half its length, and in the output it is the next-longer one, same end

reading: Output is 3x3 blocks of the input size; a block holds a copy of the input exactly where the input has its least frequent colour, else empty.

new_rows.name: rare
new_rows.datalog:
ccount(C, count(Y, X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
cmin(min(N)) :- ccount(C, N).
rare(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), ccount(C, N), cmin(M), N = M.

why: block (i,j) is the input iff input cell (i,j) has the least frequent colour, otherwise 0
invariants: the unit is the unchanged input

reading: The coloured rows at the top are reflected to the bottom, making the grid symmetric about its horizontal midline.
why: output is symmetric about the horizontal centre line; original rows kept

reading: The single marker cell fills, in its own colour, the rectangle spanning from it to the nearest grid corner.

new_rows.name: corner_box
new_rows.datalog:
hmax(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
wmax(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
mk(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
rowok(Y) :- px(Y, X, C), mk(MY, MX), hmax(H), D = H - MY, MY <= D, Y <= MY.
rowok(Y) :- px(Y, X, C), mk(MY, MX), hmax(H), D = H - MY, MY > D, Y >= MY.
colok(X) :- px(Y, X, C), mk(MY, MX), wmax(W), D = W - MX, MX <= D, X <= MX.
colok(X) :- px(Y, X, C), mk(MY, MX), wmax(W), D = W - MX, MX > D, X >= MX.
corner_box(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), rowok(Y), colok(X).

why: every cell between the marker and the closest grid corner (inclusive) has the marker colour; nothing else changes
